e-5479.knowledge_point: Finding the Characteristic Equation of a Matrix
e-5479.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/901d3a22065b48a8076b9c9aae5563c770c36c9ad40e4063c0f739847e1cda98.png)
e-5479.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\, A-\lambda I\mathbin{:}$
﻿﻿﻿![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/0c6f9f860a1cf4d510f6c3d4d9c66b77496a354bb1e2cef1b69fd1178e4f15ab.png)

Then, the characteristic equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 4 \\ 3 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-4\cdot 3 & =0 \\ 4-4\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-12 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda -8 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

e-5481.knowledge_point: Computing the Eigenvalues of a Matrix With Two Distinct Eigenvalues
e-5481.problem: Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/a1b88b7897649bb059cef39d40b2b052a13ac28282223b5688a1bce98296fb53.png)
e-5481.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $A - \lambda I\mathbin{:}$
﻿﻿![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/ca8f02e390e338b62956302ec45ea274ad73a51dafde3fe93b3d1e37dd663699.png)

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $\det(A-\lambda I) = 0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}10-\lambda  & 3 \\ 6 & 7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (10-\lambda )(7-\lambda )-3\cdot 6 & =0 \\ 70-7\lambda -10\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-18 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-17\lambda +52 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{17\pm \sqrt{(-17)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 52}}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{17\pm \sqrt{81}}{2} \\  & =\frac{17\pm 9}{2} \\  & =13,4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda=13$ and $\lambda=4.$

e-5480.knowledge_point: Computing the Eigenvalues of a Matrix With At Most One Distinct Eigenvalue
e-5480.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/5ca3e07cfbe9e5d4956b1eab4393601f2a78b0b067d17312e71cbac993e28a86.png)
e-5480.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $B-\lambda I\mathbin{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/fdbcc62870aefab6214b2f24f53e9bc5654e5386639d4bc328dff3769aff2b45.png)

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $\det(B-\lambda I) = 0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-0\cdot 0 & =0 \\ (\lambda -4)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix $B$ has only one eigenvalue $\lambda=4,$ which is a double root of the characteristic equation. 

**Note:** We also say that $\lambda=4$ has an **algebraic multiplicity** of $2.$

e-5482.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a Triangular/Diagonal Matrix
e-5482.problem: Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/603c59d43e3be000931e7279ac4d27be8aa92692f1528ec57ebd52172affa3cb.png)
e-5482.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $A - \lambda I \mathbin{:}$
﻿﻿﻿![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/f91e4886c58db10f60fa666a870aed3c2f456b25e6afb560f857e9c36e81217c.png)

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $\det (A - \lambda I) = 0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 0 \\ 9 & -2\sqrt{3}-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(-2\sqrt{3}-\lambda )-9\cdot 0 & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)(\lambda +2\sqrt{3}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the eigenvalues $\lambda={\color{red}3}$ and $\lambda={\color{blue}-2\sqrt{3}}.$

If we look again at the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/aa89b93c6fabd2f3dc7063c85e253ded7482018a5f1c6dadedc74964194c5754.png)
we see that the eigenvalues are the entries on the main diagonal. This is true in general: the eigenvalues of a *triangular* or *diagonal* matrix are *always* given by the entries on the main diagonal!

**Watch out!** For a general matrix (which is neither triangular nor diagonal), this might not be the case!

after.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -1 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Then, the characteristic equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -1 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-0\cdot (-1) & =0 \\ 5-5\lambda -\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+0 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +5 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -1 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Then, the characteristic equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -1 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-0\cdot (-1) & =0 \\ 5-5\lambda -\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+0 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +5 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 3
?

Find the characteristic equation of the matrix N=[−233−1].

a
λ2+3λ−7=0
b
λ2+λ+9=0
c
λ2−λ+7=0
d
λ2+λ−7=0
e
λ2+3λ−9=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The characteristic equation is det(N−λI)=0. Thus (−2−λ)(−1−λ)−3·3=λ²+3λ−7=0, matching option a.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Find the characteristic equation of the matrix $N=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,N-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
N-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 3 \\ 3 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Then, the characteristic equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(N-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 3 \\ 3 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )-3\cdot 3 & =0 \\ 2+2\lambda +\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-9 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda -7 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 4
?

Find the characteristic equation of the matrix D=[5−54−7].

a
λ2+2λ−15=0
b
λ2+2λ−5=0
c
λ2+2λ+15=0
d
λ2−15λ+2=0
e
λ2−2λ−5=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The characteristic equation is det(D−λI)=0. Expanding gives (5−λ)(−7−λ)−(−5)(4)=λ²+2λ−15=0, matching option a.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$D=[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 \\ 4 & -7\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,D-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
D-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -5 \\ 4 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Then, the characteristic equation is 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(D-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -5 \\ 4 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )(-7-\lambda )-(-5)\cdot 4 & =0 \\ -35-5\lambda +7\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+20 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda -15 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find the characteristic equation of the matrix B=[806−5].

a
λ2−λ−40=0
b
λ2−3λ−40=0
c
λ2−4λ+10=0
d
λ2−3λ+40=0
e
λ2+λ−10=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The characteristic equation is det(B−λI)=0. Thus (8−λ)(−5−λ)−0·6=λ²−3λ−40=0, matching option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ 6 & -5\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 0 \\ 6 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Then, the characteristic equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 0 \\ 6 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (8-\lambda )(-5-\lambda )-6\cdot 0 & =0 \\ -40-8\lambda +5\lambda +{\lambda }^{2} & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda -40 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$M=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $M-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
M-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & 5 \\ 5 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(M-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & 5 \\ 5 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-4-\lambda )(-4-\lambda )-5\cdot 5 & =0 \\ 16+4\lambda +4\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-25 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+8\lambda -9 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-8\pm \sqrt{{8}^{2}+4\cdot 1\cdot 9}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-8\pm \sqrt{100}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-8\pm 10}{2} \\  & =1,-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =1$ and $\lambda =-9.$

content.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$S=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 4 \\ -5 & 4\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $S-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
S-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-8-\lambda  & 4 \\ -5 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(S-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(S-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-8-\lambda  & 4 \\ -5 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-8-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-4\cdot (-5) & =0 \\ -32+8\lambda -4\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+20 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda -12 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{{4}^{2}+4\cdot 1\cdot 12}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{64}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm 8}{2} \\  & =-6,2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =-6$ and $\lambda =2.$

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Eigenvalues of a Matrix With Two Distinct Eigenvalues
content.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$L=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $L-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
L-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 2 \\ 5 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(L-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(L-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 2 \\ 5 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )-5\cdot 2 & =0 \\ -2+\lambda -2\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-10 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -12 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{1\pm \sqrt{(-1)^{2}+4\cdot 1\cdot 12}}{2} \\  & =\frac{1\pm \sqrt{49}}{2} \\  & =\frac{1\pm 7}{2} \\  & =-3,4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =-3$ and $\lambda =4.$

after.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$D=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $D-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿

$$
D-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(D-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(D-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(3-\lambda )-2\cdot 2 & =0 \\ 9-3\lambda -3\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{6\pm \sqrt{(-6)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 5}}{2} \\  & =\frac{6\pm \sqrt{16}}{2} \\  & =\frac{6\pm 4}{2} \\  & =5,1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =5$ and $\lambda =1.$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix 
$Q=[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $Q-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
Q-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 7 \\ 7 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(Q-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Q-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 7 \\ 7 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-7\cdot 7 & =0 \\ 4-2\lambda -2\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-49 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda -45 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}+4\cdot 1\cdot 45}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{196}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 14}{2} \\  & =-5,9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =-5$ and $\lambda =9.$

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -4 \\ 16 & 12\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & -4 \\ 16 & 12-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(B-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & -4 \\ 16 & 12-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-4-\lambda )(12-\lambda )-16\cdot (-4) & =0 \\ -48+4\lambda -12\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+64 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-8\lambda +16 & =0 \\ (\lambda -4)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Eigenvalues of a Matrix With At Most One Distinct Eigenvalue
content.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -4 \\ 16 & 12\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & -4 \\ 16 & 12-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(B-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & -4 \\ 16 & 12-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-4-\lambda )(12-\lambda )-16\cdot (-4) & =0 \\ -48+4\lambda -12\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+64 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-8\lambda +16 & =0 \\ (\lambda -4)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix $B$ has only one eigenvalue $\lambda =4,$ which is a double root of the characteristic equation.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$P=[\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ -5 & 7\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 1 \\ -5 & 7-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(P-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 1 \\ -5 & 7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )(7-\lambda )-1\cdot (-5) & =0 \\ 49-7\lambda -7\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+5 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-14\lambda +54 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the discriminant of the quadratic equation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =(-14)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 54 \\  & =196-216 \\  & =-20 \\  & <0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the characteristic equation does not have real solutions and therefore $P$ does not have real eigenvalues.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$Q=[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ -3 & 8\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $Q-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
Q-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 1 \\ -3 & 8-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(Q-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Q-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 1 \\ -3 & 8-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )(8-\lambda )-(-3)\cdot 1 & =0 \\ 40-5\lambda -8\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+3 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-13\lambda +43 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the discriminant of the quadratic equation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =(-13)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 43 \\  & =169-172 \\  & =-3 \\  & <0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the characteristic equation does not have real solutions and therefore $Q$ does not have real eigenvalues.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$E=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ -2 & -6\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $E-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
E-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 8 \\ -2 & -6-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(E-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(E-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 8 \\ -2 & -6-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(-6-\lambda )-(-2)\cdot 8 & =0 \\ -12-2\lambda +6\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +4 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's start by writing the matrix E−λI: ﻿﻿﻿E−λI=[2−λ8−2−6−λ].

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation det(E−λI)=0: det(E−λI)=0|2−λ8−2−6−λ|=0(2−λ)(−6−λ)−(−2)⋅8=0−12−2λ+6λ+λ2+16=0λ2+4λ+4=0(λ+2)2=0.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Eigenvalues of a Matrix With At Most One Distinct Eigenvalue
content.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$E=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ -2 & -6\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $E-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
E-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 8 \\ -2 & -6-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(E-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(E-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 8 \\ -2 & -6-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(-6-\lambda )-(-2)\cdot 8 & =0 \\ -12-2\lambda +6\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +4 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix $E$ has only one eigenvalue $\lambda =-2,$ which is a double root of the characteristic equation.

after.worked_solution:

﻿﻿﻿

$$
Q-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-6-\lambda  & -3 \\ 2 & -10-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={16}^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 66 \\  & =256-264 \\  & =-8 \\  & <0.\end{aligned}

Therefore, we conclude that the characteristic equation does not have real solutions, and therefore, $Q$ does not have real eigenvalues.

\begin{aligned}det(Q-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-6-\lambda  & -3 \\ 2 & -10-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-6-\lambda )(-10-\lambda )-(-3)\cdot 2 & =0 \\ 60+6\lambda +10\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+6 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+16\lambda +66 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the discriminant of the quadratic equation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={16}^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 66 \\  & =256-264 \\  & =-8 \\  & <0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the characteristic equation does not have real solutions, and therefore, $Q$ does not have real eigenvalues.

after.name: Question 16
after.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$N=[\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{7} & 6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $N-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
N-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{7}-\lambda  & 6 \\ 0 & 0-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(N-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(N-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{7}-\lambda  & 6 \\ 0 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-\sqrt{7}-\lambda )(-\lambda )-0\cdot 6 & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda +\sqrt{7}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =0$ and $\lambda =-\sqrt{7}.$

**Note:** The eigenvalues of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix are the entries on the main diagonal.

after.name: Question 19
after.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$N=[\begin{aligned}23 & -8 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $N-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
N-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}23-\lambda  & -8 \\ 0 & 0-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(N-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(N-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}23-\lambda  & -8 \\ 0 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (23-\lambda )(-\lambda )-0\cdot (-8) & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -23) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =0$ and $\lambda =23.$

**Note:** The eigenvalues of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix are the entries on the main diagonal.

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a Triangular/Diagonal Matrix
content.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$N=[\begin{aligned}18 & -5 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $N-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
N-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}18-\lambda  & -5 \\ 0 & 0-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(N-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(N-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}18-\lambda  & -5 \\ 0 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (18-\lambda )(-\lambda )-0\cdot (-5) & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -18) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =0$ and $\lambda =18.$

**Note:** The eigenvalues of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix are the entries on the main diagonal.
